advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reduce coupling of output-retry-exhaustion detection to the pydantic-ai message string (or add a test that pins the exact upstream message so an upgrade fails loudly).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:250: `if "Exceeded maximum output retries" not in str(exc):`
The ticket comment itself notes the message is `UnexpectedModelBehavior("Exceeded maximum output retries (N)")` — a private wording, not a typed/stable API.
advisory.finding: _run_prompted_output detects output-retry exhaustion by substring-matching the pydantic-ai exception message ('Exceeded maximum output retries' not in str(exc)). This couples rebar's error translation to an internal, unversioned human-readable message string; a pydantic-ai wording change would silently re-raise the raw UnexpectedModelBehavior instead of translating to UnretryableOutputError, regressing the INDETERMINATE-not-hollow contract.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_reask_echoes_the_models_own_faulty_prior_reply, attach an explicit small fitting usage (as the omit sibling test does) so the include path is grounded on the fit rule, not on FunctionModel's default usage.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py:154: `if inp <= 0: return None` — non-positive input_tokens => omit whole
pai_retry docstring: 'Missing / zero usage -> omit (its size cannot be proven, so it never rides the wire).'
advisory.finding: The reused test test_reask_echoes_the_models_own_faulty_prior_reply asserts the faulty turn-1 reply appears on the retry wire (`faulty in state["prompts"][1]`) but constructs the model with NO usage metadata (_capturing_model([faulty, ...]) without usages). Per _response_output_tokens, missing/zero input_tokens returns None and _wire_keeps_response omits the response WHOLE, so the assertion only passes if pydantic-ai's FunctionModel default populates a positive input_tokens — an undocumented environment assumption that contradicts the module's own 'missing/zero usage -> omit' rule.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a prompted-branch test that a `finish_reason="max_tokens"` truncation is reclassified into a bounded concision retry (parallel to the `length` case).
evidence: tests/unit/test_rp01_s2_bounded_op_oracle.py:261 uses only `{"text": "half an ans", "finish_reason": "length"}`; search of the oracle for `max_tokens` returned `(no matches)`
ABSENCE: no test in tests/unit passes `finish_reason="max_tokens"` through the prompted concision guard
src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py:106-108: `details = getattr(response, "provider_details", None)` ... `if isinstance(details, dict) and details.get("finish_reason") in _TRUNCATION_REASONS: return True`
ABSENCE: no test passes `provider_details={"finish_reason": "length"}` (or `max_tokens`) with `finish_reason=None` through the concision guard
advisory.finding: The concision guard reclassifies both `length` AND `max_tokens` finish reasons (`_TRUNCATION_REASONS = frozenset({"length", "max_tokens"})`), but no test exercises the `max_tokens` reason — every concision/truncation test uses `finish_reason="length"` only. Since `max_tokens` is the Anthropic-raw reason and the prompted branch's default config resolves to Anthropic, a regression dropping `max_tokens` from the truncation subset (making a real Anthropic over-cap turn terminal instead of a concision retry) would not be caught.
merged_from: `_response_is_truncated` has a documented SECOND layer reading `provider_details['finish_reason']` in the truncation subset — the exact pydantic-ai #5221 provider_details-only shape it exists to catch — but no test exercises a truncation signalled ONLY via provider_details. The oracle's provider_details-only test (test_provider_details_only_refusal_stays_terminal) covers refusal, not truncation. A regression removing the second layer would leave the refusal test green while silently making provider_details-only truncations terminal instead of concision retries.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a table-driven variant of test_truncation_is_reclassified_into_a_bounded_concision_retry parametrized over both `length` and `max_tokens` finish reasons.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a wire-projection test that a tool-calling ModelResponse is kept on the retry wire even when its usage would fail the fit rule (never omitted / never orphaning its tool return).
evidence: ABSENCE: no test constructs a ModelResponse with a ToolCallPart and non-fitting usage and asserts _make_wire_projection keeps it on the wire
advisory.finding: `_is_failed_output_response` returns False for any response carrying a `ToolCallPart`, so the wire projection ALWAYS keeps a tool-calling response regardless of the fit rule (documented: dropping it would orphan the paired tool return). No test drives a tool-calling `ModelResponse` through the projection to confirm it is retained even when its usage would fail the include-fit check — a regression that treated a tool-call turn as a projection candidate (and omitted it on size) would orphan the tool return and go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend test_unknown_count_response_is_omitted_but_retained_in_full_history-style unit to include a ModelResponse carrying a ToolCallPart with over-window usage and assert its content survives proc([...]).
